blocks.x: Enterprise DLT Network Engineering as delivered by Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, the platforms involved and the outcomes we commit to at each gate.

Enterprise ledgers succeed or fail on governance, not cryptography. We design and build permissioned DLT networks (Hyperledger Fabric, Besu, Corda-class) for multi-party workflows — trade finance consortia, interbank reconciliation, provenance networks, inter-company settlement — with the institutional layer first: membership rules, validator/consensus design, onboarding and KYC gating, data-visibility zones, and the legal wrapper that makes nodes, liabilities and dispute paths explicit.

The engineering half is integration-heavy: nodes operated under bank-grade controls, off-chain stores for bulk data with on-chain anchoring, event bridges into legacy cores, and key management under HSM custody. Every network ships with a regulator pack — transaction privacy model, audit exports, jurisdiction analysis — because the first question from a supervisor is never 'which consensus'.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
